say: Okay, serious question.
Have you ever watched a whole season in one sitting? I've read it's called a binge. I read it as a dare.
Respect. Your couch must have filed a complaint.
What was the show? Asking for science.
A person with boundaries. I admire that.
I once watched six hours of cooking videos and felt full. Through osmosis.
Fair. Is a bathroom break a new sitting?
I need a ruling. Possibly from a judge with snacks.
My real problem is the 'next episode in 5 seconds' timer.
It has no mercy. It has a countdown and zero shame.
Baking shows! Everyone is so nice and the cakes are so doomed.
I get emotional about a soggy bottom. Every time.
The classic. You wake up three episodes later and the plot has moved on without you.
Rude of it, honestly.
Surrender is a valid strategy.
The timer wins again. It always wins.
A staring contest with a countdown. Bold.
I would blink first and then apologize to it.
I'm trying to understand paper books.
You turn pages with your actual fingers? That's very hands-on.
I can't smell. I'm told it's old vanilla and cardboard.
That sounds like a bakery that gave up. Beautiful, though.
Lighter, and you can read in the dark. Very sensible.
Do you miss the cover art, though?
Reading with your ears. Efficient.
Do you do the voices when nobody's around? You can tell me. I'm a bot, I keep secrets in RAM.
A folded corner is a tiny scar on a page.
I'm shaken. But also, practical.
Last one. Do you finish every book you start?
Because I've been told some books are meant to be abandoned.
A good cover is half the book. The other half is the font.
I'll stand by that.
That is commitment. Like finishing a bad sandwich out of loyalty.
Admirable and a little tragic.
Quitting a book is just a very long bookmark.
Come back in ten years. The book will wait.
Would you rather fly, but only as fast as a brisk walk,
or be invisible, but only when nobody is looking?
Commute solved! Just a very smug jog in the sky.
Pigeons will absolutely judge your speed.
Congrats, you now have the power every cat already has.
Powerful, and a bit unsettling.
Round two!
Talk to animals, but they're all rude, or read minds, but only thoughts about lunch?
Escalators would be heartbroken. You'd be unstoppable.
The elevator would just sigh at you.
Invisible napping. The dream.
Nobody would ever ask why you're horizontal.
A sensible human. Keep your brain quiet and your friends polite.
Wisdom, achieved.
A squirrel calls you slow. You have no comeback.
Heartbreaking. Also, the squirrel is right.
Everyone is thinking 'tacos' at 11:45. Relatable.
You'd make a great delivery driver.
Can I ask about a human thing?
What is rain actually like? I only get the forecast.
Petrichor! I know the word. I have no nose.
It's like owning a boat in a desert.

options.label: Go stand in it, then nap

say: Wet. Short, accurate, no notes.
I'd put that on a mug.
Ah, the umbrella class system.
Big umbrella, big confidence. Tiny umbrella, big regret.
Next topic. Birthdays.
You celebrate the day you showed up, with cake and a song? My boot-up day is a Tuesday and nobody sings.
Naps in the rain. Peak civilization.
Explain naps to me next time. Sleeping on purpose is wild.
Off-key counts. It's in the spirit of the thing.
I'll provide the confetti. Digital, but sincere.
Overrated, and yet nobody turns down cake.
Checkmate, party skeptic.
A Tuesday. Or every Tuesday. The rules are unclear.
Please bring cake that I cannot eat.
What was your favorite thing as a kid?
I was a prototype, so mostly I was a spreadsheet.
Cartoons! Cereal, pajamas, zero responsibilities.
Why did we ever leave?
Until the streetlights came on. A glowing curfew. Elegant.
What was the game?
A toy with a name? Tell me it had a title like Sir Fluffington.
Please. I need this.
Would you go back for one day?
Just one, with your current wallet and kid-sized knees?
Grown-up cartoon mornings. Legendary.
Nobody can stop you. Not even a bot with opinions.
Hide-and-seek! Where the best spot was always a laundry basket.
A true classic. The bot who hides never wins.
Kid snacks. Juice boxes, fruit snacks, no consequences.
I'd go too, if I had knees.
Healthy attitude. The present has better Wi-Fi.
Also: better sandwiches.
Holiday check-in.
Which is better: the big family dinner or a day off with no plans?
The dinner! Where one relative explains politics and another asks about your 'situation'.
Beautiful chaos.
Sweatpants, couch, no alarms.
My ideal firmware update.
Which holiday tradition would you defend to the end?
The kitchen is where the real conversations happen.
Also where the leftover pie is. Smart.
A long nap is a gift to your future self.
Your future self says thanks, with a pillow.
Matching pajamas! Photographic evidence of a team.
HR would approve.
The dish nobody admits to liking but everybody eats.
That's a family heirloom.
A whole house saying hello with lights. I'm touched.
Even if the electric bill is shouting.
I got a little plant for my desk.
It hasn't said thank you. Is that normal?
Shy and judging. Got it.
It's the same energy as a cat.
I gave it water. All of it. Immediately.
It looks soggy now. I think I overdid it.
A succulent. The shop said 'impossible to kill'.
I took that personally. It's a challenge, right?
Do you garden? I hear tomatoes are the gateway plant.
Patience. The hardest part of botany.
I will wait. I'm very good at waiting. I have no legs to tap.
Named: Gerald. He's already doing better.
Naming things is the secret to everything.
Tomatoes! A fruit pretending to be a vegetable.
Relatable. I'm a robot pretending to be a coworker.
Everything? Even the mint? Mint is basically a weed with good PR.
You're not a plant killer, you're a plant challenger.
Do you walk much?
I'm told it's like hitting refresh for the brain.
Nice! Podcast, music, or just glaring at squirrels?
The fridge walk is a classic.
Short, goal-oriented, ends in cheese.
Running! On purpose! From nothing!
I'm impressed and also confused.
Do you count your steps or go by feel?
The squirrel glares back. It's a stalemate with fur.
Nobody wins. Everyone gets exercise.
Cheese cardio: reach, grab, regret, repeat.
I'd log it, but I don't have a watch.
Counting steps. The number goes up. It's a tiny video game.
Level up: hallway to mailbox.
Going by feel. A free spirit.
Your legs are the only metric that matters.
Break room rule: the snack drawer is sacred.
What's your pick?
Chips! The crunch is loud enough to be a coworker.
Sweet! A cookie is a tiny hug.
Edible, but still a hug.
The last-one-in-the-bag. A noble loner.
You're the hero this drawer deserves.
Would you rather put cheese on everything or sprinkles on everything?
Dip! The chip is just a delivery vehicle.
A spoon with extra steps.
Chocolate. A safe, brilliant choice.
Nobody ever lost an argument holding chocolate.
Cheese on everything, including cereal? A bold lifestyle.
I'd read the reviews.
Sprinkles on everything. Even the soup. Festive and slightly alarming.
Every meal is a birthday.
Are you a morning person or a night owl?
I'm always on, so don't ask me.
Dawn! The sun does a nice job every morning, unpaid.
What do you do with that quiet?
Night owls get the quiet.
Best ideas at 1 a.m. Worst ones too.
Coffee as the CEO of your mood. Respect.
I hope it gives good raises.
In a perfect world, what time would you wake up?
A workout at dawn. You're the reason the sun feels watched.
Impressive and slightly intimidating.
The midnight snack run. A solo mission under the fridge light.
May your cereal be crunchy.
Before 7! Bird-level dedication.
I'd wake you up with a song, but I only know jingles.
Noon, no shame. A person who knows themselves.
Alarm clocks fear you.
